topic: Military tech - submarine anechoic tiles (rubber tiles soak up sonar)
question: WHY IS IT COVERED
IN RUBBER TILES?
answer_full: To hide from sonar. They're called anechoic tiles
recap: Many modern submarines are covered in thousands of black rubber tiles.
explain: Warships and planes hunt submarines with sonar: they send out a ping of sound and listen for the echo bouncing back off the hull.
The rubber tiles are full of tiny air pockets that soak up those pings, so much less sound comes back. They also muffle the noise coming from inside the submarine.
That's why they're called anechoic tiles, which means without echo. And if the sea rips a few off, the shipyard simply glues on new ones.
